reason: Two races in the harness turn lifecycle (src/nebula/v3/harnesses.py only). (1) Stop: cancel_turn read the harness turn, its chat turn or run, and its session and wrote each with the revision it had read, while the turn's producer saves its own bookkeeping on the same rows (owner start after connecting and after each released approval, session running, tools, usage); a producer write in between failed the Stop with 'revision conflict' after the turn was already saved cancelled, leaving the chat turn routing, the producer running and the vendor turn uninterrupted. In the mirror case the producer's start bookkeeping, which ran before the guarded region, failed or was cancelled and left the session's live-turn slot taken, so the session stayed busy and the next message was forked into a new vendor session. Each Stop write is now repeated on the record's newest revision (bounded); the producer saves turn and session as running in one unit and ends quietly when Stop saved the turn first; the owner start re-reads a moved owner; the live-turn slot is released on every producer exit. (2) Failure reason: stream_turn saved a failed turn's terminal status before its error event and followers end on the terminal status, so the chat stream's error frame had no reason_code and the non-stream envelope a different error_id than the ledger. The error event is now saved first and follow_turn reads the ledger once more after the terminal status. Selected: the new deterministic regression file (all 11 cases fail on origin/main: each places one writer exactly between the other's read and write, or stops the producer inside its start bookkeeping); the Codex turn-outcome, stopped-turn, single-active-chat, connection-state and Butler recovery suites (Stop, failure and follow paths); and, by name, the harness runtime tests that drive a turn through start, Stop, failure, approval, steering, missions and restart, and the harness goal tests that stop, fail or retry a turn. Four of the selected tests are red on origin/main because of these defects and green here: the two error-frame tests and the two Stop tests. Two existing tests are repaired without changing what they assert: the Stop test awaited start_chat_turn's coroutine instead of the producer task it returns (async since #939), and the steering test read the last ledger event although the producer appends its own events after the guidance (red in 6 of 12 runs on origin/main under load).
exclusions: tests/v3/test_harnesses.py and tests/v3/test_harness_chat_goals.py are selected by name: 17 cases of the first and 2 of the second fail identically on pristine origin/main (22b46bf) and on this branch (test fixtures not updated for #939's async store; owned by the red-suites repair work), and the rest of both files does not reach the changed start, Stop, failure or follow code beyond what the selected cases cover. The two parametrized test_cyber_policy_refusal_does_not_route_or_retry_goal cases are left out only because their node ids contain spaces; they pass on both. tests/v3/test_harness_chat_goals.py::test_operator_interruption_pauses_harness_goal is left out although this change fixes its failure on origin/main (ConflictError in cancel_turn, every run): on this branch it passed 22 of 22 runs alone but failed once inside a whole-file run under load average 60+ with 'goal did not reach paused'. An in-process replica reproduced that in 2 of 726 attempts: the turn and chat turn were saved cancelled, but the stopped producer's cleanup then waited more than 20 s on a database operation, so the goal's pause came late or not at all. The cause is not established (it could not be reproduced with a thread dump); it is reported in the PR as an open limitation rather than selected as reliably green. Not selected because they fail identically on origin/main and on this branch for unrelated reasons: test_claude_harness_turns.py, test_harness_provider_subagents.py, test_harness_activity_cost.py, test_harness_leftovers.py, test_grok_acp_compliance.py, test_approval_continuation.py, test_turn_outcome_history.py, test_universal_agent_tools.py (same failing cases on both checkouts). No process-level tests are selected: the change is in the in-process harness runtime. No frontend, native or Playwright cases: no UI code, API shape or setting changed. Real-Core evidence (scratch supervisor Core on PostgreSQL with an inert Codex stand-in: 5 of 5 failed turns carried the ledger's reason_code and error_id on the stream; 9 of 9 Stops at three moments answered 200 and released the session) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI. No real harness account, live Core or deployment was used.
